back: A short statement of the overall purpose and values of an organisation.
An aim is a broad long-term goal. An objective is a specific, measurable target that normally has a time limit.
Mission statement, aims, objectives, strategy, tactics: each level supports the one above.
Strategic: long term, set by directors. Tactical: medium term, set by middle managers. Operational: day to day, set by supervisors.
Survival, profit (and profit maximisation), growth, market share, social and environmental goals, and service.
Judging a business on economic, social and environmental results, not only on profit.
Acceptance by a firm of its duty to act in the interests of society. Benefits: reputation and loyalty. Costs: higher expenses.
Profit against social goals, growth against quality, market share against margin: managers must prioritise.
Stage of the business, changes in the economy, competition, technology or law, new owners or managers, and results against target.
